commits.message:
feat(renderer): a statusline request is answered through Renderer.answer, in process (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2xo) (#711)

* feat(renderer): a statusline request is answered through Renderer.answer, in process, by the present its turn returns (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2xo)

* fix(renderer): review high — overlapping turns stated, one logfmt field type, the answer's settle holds only what it records (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2xo)

- The interface no longer claims one input at a time: a request's turn waits
  inside itself until the mailbox holds that wait, so turns overlap.
- The host decides once whether it records a turn, and builds its line only
  when it does.
- One logfmt field type and one event-line writer serve the request event and
  the turn line.
- The settle a request's answer returns is built outside the draw, so it no
  longer keeps the draw's setup alive until its frame settles.
- The rate-limit vocabulary is back beside the function that produces it.
- The doctor's can-move text names a moving bar handed off to another lane,
  which the client's sighting now reads as the handoff line it drew.

* fix(renderer): review medium — every exit after a render's answer settles its present, one failure-message spelling, true seam claims (candybar-host-renderer-x96a.2xo)

- A sighting or request-event write that throws after the answer settles the
  present failed before the throw reaches the connection, so the renderer
  keeps no record of a reply that was never sent.
- A turn's failure reaches the client through renderFailed's one extraction,
  with the renderer and what it was doing in front.
- The interface and the session context say what holds: they import only
  types. The renderer's turn record no longer claims the renderer writes no
  log; the host parts it reaches name the wait's log among what the mailbox
  takes away.
